sonnet.problem: The story card says David 'looks at how long people last', which states what the breath picture means. The text doesn't say it. It also hands the baker the answer to the true/false card that follows.
sonnet.rule: Leave open what the text leaves open. This includes what a picture means. He retells the picture as the text gives it and says what it stands for only when the passage says so.

sonnet.problem: The true/false statement ('life doesn't last') just restates the setup in card 7 ('how long people last'). It is trivially true and asks nothing new.
sonnet.rule: A True statement never just repeats the card before it.

sonnet.problem: The question asks what the 'plants nurtured in their youth' picture means, and the right answer ('growing strong') is the card's own interpretation. The passage doesn't say what the picture stands for.
sonnet.rule: Leave open what the text leaves open. This includes what a picture means. He retells the picture as the text gives it and says what it stands for only when the passage says so.

sonnet.problem: The joke says the Millers' kitchen is where Papa Dorin 'came from'. His backstory says he came from a bakery bin and was bought for 25 cents. The Millers' kitchen is where he lived. The joke contradicts his backstory.
sonnet.rule: His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery, the junk drawer and the Millers' kitchen. They fit the backstory, never change it, and don't contradict each other in one lesson.

sonnet.problem: The question asks the baker to infer what 'great loads' tells us ('there's plenty to haul'). The text gives no such reason or meaning, so the right answer adds a reason the passage doesn't state.
sonnet.rule: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.
